audit_findings.title: Possible double counting of equity-method investments
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.639 million LTM equity-method loss, computed from $5.008 million fiscal-2025 income less $8.205 million prior-year Q1 income plus $0.442 million current-Q1 loss; 3.2% of the $114.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method results may remain in net income-based OE while the $119.3 million investment carrying value is separately added through the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our proportionate share of equity method investments was income of $ 5.0 million in fiscal 2025 and a loss of $ 11 million in both fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023, which is included on the consolidated statements of income.
audit_findings.explanation: No double counting is demonstrated because the OE reconciliation was not supplied. The current LTM equity-method result is a loss, so retaining it would understate rather than overstate the anchor. Removing $3.639 million would change base value by approximately $2.20 per share using the supplied operating-PV-to-anchor ratio, leaving the $76.59 base value far below the $147.99 market price.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the complete net-income-to-OE reconciliation for equity-method income, losses and distribution gains; remove them consistently before adding stakes_net.

audit_findings.title: Zero reported NCI may conceal future partner claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 recognized NCI at January 31, 2026; all seven third-party Member LLC interests were withdrawn in May 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: A partner waterfall could divert consolidated OE from RH common shareholders, requiring an attribution adjustment to OE or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 31, 2026, of the remaining seven Member LLCs, we hold a 50 percent membership interest in six of the Member LLCs, and the remaining noncontrolling interest of 50 percent in each Member LLC is held by the same development partner.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms that the partners had no claim under the waterfalls at January 31, and the subsequent May 2026 transaction eliminated their Member LLC interests before the valuation date. Therefore, the identified future partner claim does not remain outstanding, although accounting for the asset-separation transaction was still being evaluated.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the May 2026 closing statements and final accounting to confirm there is no contingent consideration, residual waterfall right or surviving obligation; update the bridge separately for any transaction-accounting changes.

audit_findings.title: Landlord-asset construction may be missing from reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $109.789 million LTM cash outflow, computed from $89.028 million fiscal 2025 less $17.800 million prior-year Q1 plus $38.561 million current Q1; maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted landlord-asset construction cash outflows would reduce OE through the reinvestment deduction and therefore reduce every scenario's operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: We define adjusted capital expenditures as capital expenditures from investing activities and cash outflows of capital related to construction activities to design and build landlord-owned leased assets, net of tenant allowances received during the construction period.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved calculation issue, not a demonstrated omission. The LTM cash outflow equals 96.1% of the $114.2 million anchor, so even a materially smaller maintenance component could substantially change the valuation. The full amount cannot automatically be deducted because the record does not separate maintenance from growth investment.
audit_findings.action: Trace landlord-assets-under-construction cash outflows and tenant allowances into every annual OE calculation, classify maintenance versus growth amounts, and rerun all scenarios for any omitted maintenance component.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease amortization can create a false add-back
audit_findings.magnitude: $65.408 million LTM finance-lease ROU amortization, computed from $62.875 million fiscal 2025 less $14.673 million prior-year Q1 plus $17.206 million current Q1; actual incorrect add-back unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding finance-lease ROU amortization back as D&A without deducting principal or an equivalent replacement charge inflates OE and its capitalized operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating lease costs and amortization of finance lease right-of-use assets are included in cost of goods sold or selling, general and administrative expenses on the consolidated statements of income based on our accounting policy.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that finance-lease amortization exists and is recurring, but the supplied record does not establish whether it was included in eligible D&A. The LTM amount equals 57.3% of the $114.2 million anchor, making a classification error reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the D&A add-back schedule, exclude finance-lease ROU amortization or introduce an economically equivalent recurring lease-capital charge, and rerun the OE series and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Signed but uncommenced leases are absent from the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $578 million of legally binding uncommenced lease payments at May 2, 2026, including $17 million during the remainder of fiscal 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Future rent, pre-opening costs and ramp losses will reduce projected OE and growth unless offset by incremental revenue and margin from the new locations.
audit_findings.evidence: Total lease payments exclude $ 645 million of legally binding payments under the non-cancellable term for leases signed but not yet commenced under our accounting policy as of January 31, 2026, of which $ 26 million, $ 34 million, $ 36 million, $ 39 million and $ 40 million are expected to be paid in fiscal 2026, fiscal 2027, fiscal 2028, fiscal 2029 and fiscal 2030, respectively, and $ 470 million will be paid subsequent to fiscal 2030.
audit_findings.explanation: These commitments are filed and substantial, but their omission from historical OE is not an accounting error because the leases had not commenced. Their value effect depends on the unknown earnings and cash generation of the associated locations, so gross lease payments cannot be treated as a valuation loss.
audit_findings.action: Build location-level opening schedules with rent, pre-opening expense, working capital, revenue and margin ramps; verify that scenario growth rates are net of these incremental costs.

audit_findings.title: Unhedged floating-rate interest can materially change OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $24 million of annual interest expense per 100-basis-point rate change, equal to 21.0% of the $114.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Because interest remains in equity-level OE, future benchmark rates and refinancing spreads directly change projected OE rather than the debt bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on the average interest rate on the revolving line of credit under the ABL Credit Agreement and the Term Loan B and Term Loan B-2 under the Term Loan Credit Agreement during fiscal 2025, and to the extent that borrowings were outstanding under any facility, for every 100-basis point change in interest rates, our annual interest expense could change by approximately $24 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The current anchor includes prevailing interest expense, so no historical error is demonstrated. Future rate movements are not presently in the numbers and could raise or lower value materially; the filed sensitivity is large relative to anchor OE.
audit_findings.action: Rerun bear, base and bull projections using facility-level balances, SOFR paths, contractual floors and margins, scheduled amortization, and October 2028 refinancing assumptions.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $41.7 million computed fiscal-2021 residual, based on $58.3 million identified as 58.3% of filed D&A
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual proven to be eligible non-economic D&A would be added back to historical OE.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2021 $58.3m (58.3% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The uncertainty is conservative, but the supplied residual relates only to fiscal 2021. The valuation anchors to latest actual 2026 OE rather than a trend, so correcting fiscal 2021 would not change the $114.2 million anchor. Raising 2021 OE from $183.7 million by at most $41.7 million also would not resolve the series' $699.0 million peak and $5.7 million trough.
audit_findings.action: Classify the fiscal-2021 residual from filed asset-level disclosures; rerun the valuation only if eligible residual D&A is also identified in the latest anchor period or changes the anchor-selection rule.
